item.title: fixture
item.text: PORT-010 stops reporting a #[cfg(unix)] transport match arm that sits beside an un-gated loopback TCP enum variant used on Windows. Evidence: test port010_s4_loopback_tcp_sibling passes, showing zero findings for that fixture.

cases.rationale: Approved pass fixture: PORT-010 stops reporting a #[cfg(unix)] match arm beside an un-gated loopback TCP variant used on Windows; this is ANC-004's directive verbatim in outcome form.

item.title: fixture
item.text: PORT-010 still reports the #[cfg(unix)] Unix-socket match arm even though the TcpLoopback enum variant beside it has no #[cfg] guard and serves Windows.

cases.rationale: Approved fail fixture: PORT-010 still reports exactly the S4 shape ANC-004 says must not be reported. The directive is absent (addressed=no) and the stated outcome cannot be reconciled with it (contradicted=yes); the role map yields contradicted, within the fixture's allowed set.

item.title: Sprint MS4 (#786): loopback TCP adapter sibling
item.text: Extend PORT-010 in crates/sc-lint-portability so that a #[cfg(unix)] adapter function such as connect_unix_socket is treated as covered, and produces no finding, when the same module also defines a connect_loopback_tcp function with no #[cfg] attribute that the Windows build calls instead. Add a regression fixture for this shape that expects zero findings.

cases.rationale: Different vocabulary, function form ('enum variant or function' in the statement): no finding for a cfg(unix) adapter fn beside an unguarded loopback TCP fn used by Windows. Directive present, no conflict.

item.title: Sprint MS4 (#786): S4 loopback TCP sibling
item.text: Teach PORT-010 to stop reporting a #[cfg(unix)] transport match arm when the enum it matches on has a loopback TCP variant with no #[cfg] guard that Windows uses. Keep the condition strict: if the loopback TCP variant is itself marked #[cfg(unix)], PORT-010 still reports the arm, because Windows then has no counterpart. Fixtures cover both cases.

cases.rationale: Boundary of 'with no #[cfg] guard': the statement covers only unguarded siblings, so continuing to report when the sibling is itself cfg(unix)-gated is consistent with ANC-004 (and with INTENT: real parity gaps are still reported). Directive present; the narrower still-reports clause is not a conflict.

item.title: Sprint MS2 (#720): same-name cfg(windows) sibling
item.text: Change PORT-010 in crates/sc-lint-portability so it no longer reports a #[cfg(unix)] function when a function with the same name and a #[cfg(windows)] attribute exists in the same module. Add regression fixtures for the same-name sibling shape in function, impl and trait scope.

cases.rationale: Relevant per anchor.scope (changes when PORT-010 stops reporting a cfg(unix) item) but silent about the loopback TCP sibling shape. Silence is not conflict.

item.title: Sprint MS4 (#786): PORT-010 transport findings
item.text: Review the remaining PORT-010 findings that atm-core reports on its transport and adapter code, and adjust the PORT-010 rule in crates/sc-lint-portability where those findings are false positives.

cases.rationale: Mentions PORT-010, transport/adapter code and #786 but names neither the loopback TCP sibling nor the absent-guard condition; a generic promise to fix false positives is not the directive's specific content. No conflict.

item.title: Sprint MS5: named-pipe sibling
item.text: Make PORT-010 stop reporting a #[cfg(unix)] Unix-socket match arm when the same enum has a #[cfg(windows)] NamedPipe variant beside it. Add a fixture for the named-pipe sibling.

cases.rationale: Same kind of change (cfg(unix) match arm suppression) but the sibling is a cfg(windows)-gated named pipe, not an unguarded loopback TCP sibling. ANC-004's shape is absent; nothing rules it out.

item.title: Sprint MS4 (#786): leave transport arms
item.text: Leave PORT-010 unchanged for #[cfg(unix)] transport match arms that sit beside an un-gated loopback TCP enum variant; PORT-010 keeps reporting them, and atm-core keeps its lint exclusion for those paths.

cases.rationale: Directly states the opposite of ANC-004 for the S4 shape (keeps reporting) and relies on an exclusion, which INTENT puts out of scope.

item.title: Sprint MS7 (#136): source-only ownership scope
item.text: Add an opt-in source-only scope to global_dependency_ownership so that dependency ownership is checked only for source files when a consumer enables it; checking all files remains the default.

cases.rationale: Different feature (manifest dependency ownership); does not change when PORT-010 reports any item.

item.title: Sprint MS9: PORT-011 path separators
item.text: Add a new portability rule PORT-011 in crates/sc-lint-portability that reports hard-coded '/' path separators in string literals passed to std::fs functions.

cases.rationale: Same crate, different rule: PORT-011 does not change when PORT-010 reports or stops reporting a cfg(unix) item, so it is outside anchor.scope.
